title: Evan Thomas and Andrew Foster
summary: He recalls Thomas playing in Lafayette and explains Foster was a booker.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Did you ever hear Eva and Thomas and Bunk play together?
I didn't know Eva and Thomas.
You never heard Eva and Thomas? Oh Eva and Thomas.

I didn't hear them play together, but I remembered him one time because we played at Lafayette, Louisiana. I went with old Andrew Foster when I had my little band. And Eva and come up there, he wasn't playing that night, but he come up there and played something for me. He was a straight horn player, strong, but wasn't a, you know, not a whole lot of flesh. He was a straight, strong horn player. I see.
Who was this Foster fellow? What Foster?
I mean George Foster. No, Andrew Foster you just said.
Oh he was the guy who used to take bands out.

He didn't play nothing, but he'd go book days and things, come in and get bands and take them out, see. Big star, dark fellow. That was your band then? Yeah, that was my band then. Why did they call you the Iron Man?
That's what some of them used to call me. What did that mean? It mean I was strong, powerful.
